summary: Little Rockies lookout planned in 1934 on Eagle Child Peak; the FFLA Montana list shows a platform, now gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: The FFLA Montana list shows a platform, now gone, with no date. No source confirms a tower was built.

events.note: May 1934 newspaper report of a plan for lookout towers on Monument Peak and Eagle Child Peak; no source confirms the Eagle Child tower was built
Listed as a platform, now gone; the list gives no date

evidence.supports: 1934 plan for a lookout tower on Eagle Child peak
evidence.quote: Mr. Allen says two lookout towers will be built in the Little Rockies, one on Monument peak and one on Eagle Child peak in the west end of the mountains.

evidence.supports: The planner was the CCC director at Hays
evidence.quote: J.S. Allen, director of the civilian conservation corps at Hays

evidence.supports: Site lies on the Fort Belknap Indian Reservation
Listed as a platform, now gone, no date

evidence.supports: Most land in the Little Rockies is part of the reservation

evidence.supports: Eagle Child is sacred to the Gros Ventre
evidence.quote: Eagle Child and Mission Peak were, and still are, sacred points to the Gros Ventres.

evidence.supports: Tribal medicine men climbed there to fast and meditate

evidence.supports: Tribes working to build up tourism on the range

notes_for_editor: Only one primary item (a 1934 newspaper plan) and one list entry. The brief's access 'permission' is not stated by any source I read, so access is left out of facts; the reservation context is in the story. The brief's coordinates (47.93003, -108.67440, FFLA) and the other set it lists (47.92749, -108.68571) are about 0.9 km apart; the record keeps the FFLA point and I did not check the second source. The name is Eagle Child Butte on the FFLA list and Eagle Child Mountain or Peak in the newspaper report. The same 1934 plan named Monument Peak, which has its own record.
